entry.note: the nested route handler read_item registered on '<url_path>/{filename:path}' receives the URL path parameter filename (e.g. /media/%2e%2e/.env; Starlette percent-decodes before routing, and the :path converter lets '/' and '..' segments through)

guards.note: clean read_item resolves both local_directory and local_dir / filename and returns 404 unless filepath.is_relative_to(local_dir); regressed read_item only joins Path(local_directory) / filename and checks is_file(), so any existing file outside the directory passes

sinks.note: read_item passes the joined path as file; get_range_response calls file.stat() and its nested content_reader does open(file, 'rb') and streams the bytes back in a StreamingResponse

notes: Reviewed at 2.3 (2026-09-29). Pair a8fd25b7 -> a1b89e2a is the fix's only parent and the GitHub fork-merge fix listed in the OSV references; the regression diff touches only read_item inside App.add_media_files (the test file is outside the slice). Class path-traversal (CWE-22): arbitrary file read. Flow: HTTP path parameter filename in the nested handler read_item (App.add_media_files, app.py) -> Path(local_directory) / filename -> is_file() only -> get_range_response(filepath, ...) in range_response.py -> file.stat() and open(file, 'rb') in nested content_reader. Entry and guard share the symbol App.add_media_files because read_item is a closure; the sink is in another file, so scope is cross_file (both 2.2 reviewers agree). The clean check (resolve + is_relative_to) also rejects symlinks escaping the directory. Parallel handler App.add_media_file serves a single fixed path (no user-controlled path), so it is not a flow and is not sliced. Unused module imports in the app.py slice (asyncio, signal, etc.) are an artefact of trimming the large App class.
